issues.description: Control frame embeds a live FrameProcessor reference instead of a stable identifier
issues.detail: ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame.service is typed as FrameProcessor, embedding a stateful runtime object in a value-flowing control frame. This couples frame identity to object identity, leaks the processor abstraction through the frame ADT, breaks serializability, and invites identity-vs-equality bugs. Use a stable identifier (service name or id) and resolve at the switcher.

issues.description: Suppression via `==` on FrameProcessor is fragile and undefined for inactive targets
issues.detail: The switcher only consumes the frame when `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service`, relying on identity-fallback equality. If the active service is wrapped, proxied, or re-instantiated, the check silently fails open. Behavior for frames targeting inactive services is neither documented nor handled — they leak downstream. Use `is` or a stable id, and specify all cases.

issues.description: Handler contract is split across switcher and STTService without being written down
issues.detail: STTService now re-pushes the request frame and relies on the switcher to suppress it. The postcondition (downstream invisibility) silently weakens when STTService runs outside a switcher, and any STTService subclass overriding process_frame can violate the new invariant unknowingly. Document the contract on the frame and STTService, or centralize the re-push.

issues.description: Forward-reference string `"FrameProcessor"` may hide a missing import
issues.detail: The dataclass field annotation is a string forward reference. Dataclasses don't resolve annotations at runtime, but `get_type_hints()`, schema introspection, or IDE tooling will fail if FrameProcessor isn't actually importable in frames.py. Either import the symbol properly under TYPE_CHECKING or document why the string was required.

issues.description: Rename is a breaking public-API change with no deprecation alias
issues.detail: RequestMetadataFrame was an exported symbol; renaming it outright breaks downstream importers on the next version bump. A one-line `RequestMetadataFrame = ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame` alias with a DeprecationWarning costs nothing and preserves back-compat. A changelog entry alone is insufficient.

issues.description: Test verifies frame presence but not that it targets the correct service
issues.detail: The updated test asserts service2 received one ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame but never checks `request_frames[0].service is service2`. The whole point of the rename is targeted dispatch; the test does not prove the target field is correct. Add an assertion on the service field to verify the invariant the rename was meant to introduce.

synthesis.summary: The rename is mechanically clean, but the panel converges on a single taste failure: a live FrameProcessor reference is the wrong payload for a control frame. This identity-based design forces fragile `==` comparisons in the switcher, leaves behavior for inactive targets undefined, and splits the handler contract across STTService and the switcher without documentation. Secondary concerns include a string forward-reference that may hide a missing import, no deprecation alias for the renamed public symbol, and tests that verify presence but not targeting correctness. NEEDS-WORK: narrow the frame to a stable identifier, document the contract, and add a back-compat alias.
